# DACH and GDPR: a constraint that can work as an advantage

## Regulation as a head start
### Not a brake, but an advantage
### Especially for DACH
### Suited to an agent-based economy

## GDPR-by-construction
### Consent in the architecture
### A written trail by default
### Not a layer added after the fact

## Data minimization
### Parameterized questions from the agent
### Parameterized responses from the business
### Without a full user profile

## Transfer of personal data
### Only with explicit consent
### A loggable receipt
#### Exactly what was disclosed

## Model limitations
### For now, only a principle
### UX not yet defined
### Legal form remains open

## Federation of trust from the ground up
### Without a global monopolist
### Built on existing roots
### Resilience against platform capture

## Sources of authority
### Domain and certificate
### Chambers and registries
### Qualification institutions
### Natural for Baden-Württemberg

## Open question
### Readiness for cross-signing
### Institutions not yet confirmed
